title: 04. OOP: DESIGN PATTERNS
summary: DESIGN PATTERNS: explanations and runnable examples.

sections.title: Introduction

quiz.question: What are design patterns?
options: In Python, yes — it follows EAFP (Easier to Ask Forgiveness than Permission) over LBYL (Look Before You Leap).
Decorator pattern: wraps an object to add behavior, same interface.
True suppresses the exception (it won't propagate). False (or None) lets the exception propagate normally.
Reusable solutions to common software design problems. They're templates, not code — you adapt them to your specific needs.
quiz.explanation: Reusable solutions to common software design problems. They're templates, not code — you adapt them to your specific needs. Categories: Creational (Singleton, Factory, Builder), Structural (Decorator, Adapter, Facade), Behavioral (Observer, Strategy, Command).

quiz.question: When would you use Singleton?
options: DIP is the principle (depend on abstractions). DI is the technique (pass dependencies from outside).
When multiple threads/processes access shared data simultaneously and the result depends on execution order.
Percentage of code executed during tests. 80%+ is a common target.
When you need exactly ONE instance: database connection pool, logger, configuration manager, cache.
quiz.explanation: When you need exactly ONE instance: database connection pool, logger, configuration manager, cache. But use cautiously — it's essentially a global variable and makes testing harder.

quiz.question: What is the difference between Factory and Builder?
options: Pydantic: validates and coerces types automatically, generates JSON schema, has rich error reporting.
Running the same test with different inputs. @pytest.mark.parametrize lets you define multiple test cases without duplicating test code.
A User class should only manage user data. Saving to database → UserRepository.
Factory creates different types of objects through a single interface (which type).
quiz.explanation: Factory creates different types of objects through a single interface (which type). Builder constructs a complex object step by step (how to build). Factory: create("email").

quiz.question: When would you use the Strategy pattern?
options: model_dump() converts to a Python dict. model_dump_json() converts to a JSON string.
Python uses Protocols (structural typing). Small, focused protocols let classes implement only what they need.
Bottom-up for wrapping, top-down for execution. @A @B def f() → f = A(B(f)).
When you need to swap algorithms at runtime: payment methods, sorting algorithms, compression strategies, authentication methods.
quiz.explanation: When you need to swap algorithms at runtime: payment methods, sorting algorithms, compression strategies, authentication methods. Follows Open/Closed Principle.

quiz.question: What is the Observer pattern?
options: Factory creates different types of objects through a single interface (which type).
Abstracts data access behind a clean interface. Business logic talks to the repository (abstract), not the database (concrete).
@contextmanager for simple cases (less boilerplate). Class-based when you need complex state management or the context manager is reusable across multiple with blocks.
Objects subscribe to events and get notified when events occur.
quiz.explanation: Objects subscribe to events and get notified when events occur. Publishers don't know about subscribers. Used in: event systems, reactive programming, GUI frameworks.
